positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient described a traumatic event that 'shook me deeply' and caused ongoing distress. Criterion B1 (re-experiencing): MET — patient reports 'thinking about it' and 'waking up feeling shaken from dreams.' Criterion B3 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient mentions steering clear of 'certain places and conversations.' Criterion C1 (inability to recall details): MET — patient describes 'pieces missing' and a 'foggy' memory. Criterion C2 (negative beliefs): MET — patient expresses a 'dark cloud' and a belief that 'things will never improve.' Criterion C3 (blame): MET — patient reflects on blaming themselves and others for the trauma. Criterion C4 (negative emotions): MET — patient reports feelings of fear and guilt that 'just doesn’t go away.' Criterion C5 (diminished interest): MET — patient states they avoid activities they used to enjoy. Criterion C6 (detachment): MET — patient feels 'detached' and 'on the outside looking in.' Criterion C7 (inability to experience positive emotions): MET — patient finds it hard to feel happiness or satisfaction. Criterion C8 (irritability): MET — patient describes moments of 'overwhelming irritability.' Criterion C9 (recklessness): MET — patient acknowledges taking risks as a way to cope. Criterion D1 (hypervigilance): MET — patient feels 'constantly on edge.' Criterion D2 (startle response): MET — patient reports being 'more easily startled.' Criterion D3 (concentration difficulties): MET — patient struggles to focus and 'zones out.' Criterion D4 (sleep disturbances): MET — patient has 'more trouble with sleep.' Total: 14 of 14 criteria met (threshold ≥ 1). Duration: met (symptoms started after the event and have persisted for over a month).
